subject: Post-call: Genomex private deployment options and offline ops tradeoffs
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Dr. Julian Katz <julian.katz@genomex.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-09T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap — Genomex private deployment options and immediate asks

Thanks Julian — good conversation today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so everyone has the same view. If I misstated anything please flag.

Summary of requirements you shared on the call:
- Must run in an air-gapped / sealed environment inside Genomex datacenters for IP protection.
- No persistent internet egress from the inference hosts; control plane can be an isolated relay or customer-managed only.
- Expect initial footprint ~8 GPUs (A100-class equivalent) with room to scale to ~24 GPUs over 12 months.
- Upgrades/patching windows: windows are infrequent (1–2 per quarter) and must be executed with 4 hours max planned downtime; emergency patching needs an agreed on-call process.
- Storage: on-prem encrypted, KMS integration required (customer-managed HSM/KMS).
- Auditability: detailed access logs, config drift alerts, and weekly health dumps.

Open technical questions (we need answers to size the SOW / BOM):
1) Can you confirm rack-level constraints (U/rack available, power per rack, network egress point)? See attached inventory template — please fill and return.
2) Do you require hardware spares onsite (we recommend 1 GPU spare per 12 GPUs; confirm acceptance).
3) Will BiomedOps own the maintenance windows or will that be coordinated by Genomex infra?
4) Any restrictions on cryptographic modules (FIPS/HSM vendor preference)?

Immediate next steps we propose:
- Action: Genomex completes the attached HW inventory template by EOD 2028-05-12 (Owner: Genomex).
- Action: Redwood (Ben) to draft a high-level BOM and proposed rack layout based on the inventory (Due: 2028-05-15).
- Action: Redwood (Soojin) to propose offline patching playbook options (canary-first vs staged parallel racks) and runbook examples (Due: 2028-05-16).
- Action: Procurement (Genomex) to share lead times and PO process for vendor-approved hardware (Julian / procurement@example.com).

Attachments: genomex_hw_inventory_template.xlsx (fill), redwood_private_onprem_requirements_v2.pdf (reference), network_diagram_draft.png (we sketched the controlled egress patterns).

Thanks — I’ll wait for the inventory and will start sizing a BOM once we have the rack/power details.

--
Priya Natarajan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Dr. Julian Katz <julian.katz@genomex.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Genomex Procurement <procurement@genomex.ai>
Date: 2028-05-09T17:09:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Genomex private deployment options and immediate asks

Priya — thank you for the clear summary. Confirming the high-level points. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Rack constraints: two 48U racks available in the sealed zone (we estimate 20U available per rack after existing kit). Power: 60A per rack, single PDUs in redundant configuration.
- We prefer Nvidia H100 if possible; procurement will confirm model availability but A100-equivalent is acceptable.
- Spares: we can host one spare server cabinet in a warm-rack if Redwood recommends; procurement preference is to buy-through (Genomex-owned assets).
- Patching: Genomex infra team will own the scheduling but wants Redwood to provide a tested offline patch sequence.
- KMS: We have an on-prem HSM (Thales) — we will share certs and vendor details once procurement loop is in.

Julian — procurement is copied here. We will fill the inventory template and aim to return it by 2028-05-12 but may need one extra day depending on vendor confirmations.

On the commercial side: we discussed pilot pricing contours if we do a 3-month pilot on private infra vs a hosted evaluation. Would appreciate an outline of options in the BOM doc.

—Julian
Dr. Julian Katz, VP Research Ops
Genomex
julian.katz@genomex.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dr. Julian Katz <julian.katz@genomex.ai>, Genomex Procurement <procurement@genomex.ai>
Date: 2028-05-10T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Genomex private deployment options and immediate asks (technical clarifications)

Thanks Julian — helpful. A couple of technical clarifications from infra/ops perspective: 

1) Hardware & cooling assumptions: with 20U usable per rack and 60A PDUs, our recommended baseline for 8x H100-equivalent GPUs is two 2U servers (4 GPUs each) plus a management host and NVMe storage nodes. We'll include a rack diagram in the BOM. If you prefer denser blades we can adapt but that affects cooling and spares.

2) Offline patch strategy options (short notes):
  - Option A (staged canary): patch one server in each rack during a maintenance window, validate KV-cache warmup, then proceed (min downtime but longer overall).
  - Option B (parallel rolling): take a whole rack offline, failover to second rack using prefix cache priming; faster per-stage but requires capacity headroom.
  - Option C (batch upgrade with warm standby): add a warm spare machine to absorb load and perform bulk upgrades offline; higher CAPEX but shortest maintenance windows.

3) Network egress modes: we support a customer-managed relay that sits in a DMZ with an allowlist for Redwood control plane IPs, or a completely offline control plane with signed manifests transferred via removable media (airgap sync). We should decide on the acceptable tradeoff between automation and manual drift control.

Action items for Redwood (internal): Ben — prepare BOM/rack-layour with 3 profiles (CAPEX-lean, balanced, low-downtime) by 2028-05-15. Rishi — draft an offline patching playbook skeleton and backout steps by 2028-05-16. Priya — follow up on SOW language for spare hardware ownership (we need to present both buy and rent models).

I'll attach a short example playbook excerpt in the BOM deliverable.

--
Soojin Lee
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-05-11T09:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — Genomex private deployment options and immediate asks (next steps & timelines)

Julian / procurement — thanks for the confirmation and for taking the inventory task. To keep momentum: 

1) If inventory arrives by 2028-05-12 we will produce the three-profile BOM + preliminary SOW language and a pilot commercial outline by 2028-05-15.
2) If you need an extra day, we can shift the BOM to 2028-05-16 but would prefer no more than that so procurement lead time estimates are useful.
3) Please confirm whether Genomex prefers Redwood to own spares (on a managed reserve) or for Genomex to procure and own them — both options will be priced differently in the BOM.
4) For the airgap control plane: do you want an automated signed-manifest model (we provide tooling + signatures) or a manual removable-media flow? Select now so our SOW includes appropriate acceptance criteria.

Proposed check-in: 2028-05-16 10:00 PT (30min) to review BOM draft and patching choices. If that works please accept calendar invite (sending separately).

Thanks — we’ll align internal owners and have the deliverables ready once we receive the completed template.

--
